faq.q: What is the best boat for a small Ironman recovery group?
faq.a: For a group of up to 5, the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) are perfect. Both depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper, drinks, and snacks. If you have up to 8 people, the Bandido (11.5m) offers more space. For larger groups of 10-12, consider the Azimut 39 or Fairline Targa.

faq.q: Can I swim in the sea after the Ironman?
faq.a: Absolutely. The sea around Marbella is calm and warm, especially in summer. Your skipper can anchor in sheltered spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where you can float, swim gently, and let your muscles recover. Always listen to your body and stay hydrated.

faq.q: Are drinks and food included on the charter?
faq.a: Yes, every charter includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. For deeper recovery, you can bring your own electrolytes or protein bars—just let the crew know. No extra charges for standard inclusions.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book the yacht after Ironman 2051?
faq.a: Book at least 2-3 weeks ahead, especially if you want a specific boat like the Mangusta 80 or a longer 8-hour charter. Ironman week brings many visitors to Marbella, so early booking ensures availability and better time slots.

faq.q: What if I'm too tired to sail?
faq.a: You don't need to do anything—our licensed skippers handle all navigation. You can simply lie on the deck, enjoy the views of La Concha, and let the gentle motion of the boat aid your recovery. No experience required.

faq.q: Are there any extra fees for fuel or taxes?
faq.a: No. Fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%) are all included in the quoted price. The only optional extras are things like a private chef or watersports (except the free jet ski on Mangusta 80 charters).

data.body_html:
Crossing the Ironman 2051 finish line is a monumental achievement. Your body has been through hours of swimming, cycling, and running—now it deserves a recovery day that’s both restorative and memorable. A marbella yacht charter ironman 2051 recovery day from Puerto Banús offers the perfect blend of relaxation, gentle activity, and breathtaking scenery. Forget cramped hotel pools; step aboard a private yacht, let the Mediterranean work its magic, and celebrate your accomplishment in style.

Why a Yacht Is the Ultimate Ironman Recovery

After extreme endurance, your muscles need low-impact movement, hydration, and mental reset. A yacht provides all three. Floating on calm water reduces joint stress, while swimming in the sea (if you feel up to it) promotes blood flow without impact. The sun, sea air, and changing views help lower cortisol levels. Plus, you can control the pace—anchor in a quiet cove, stretch on the deck, or simply nap in the shade.

Choosing the Right Boat for Your Group

Your recovery group size dictates the best vessel. For a solo athlete or couple, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are agile and intimate. For up to 8 people, the Bandido (11.5m) offers a spacious cockpit. Groups of 10-12 will appreciate the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) or Fairline Targa (12m, 10 pax). If you want to splurge, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski—perfect for a support crew member to have fun while you recover.

Pricing That Fits Your Post-Race Budget

We keep pricing transparent. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are our Tier A boats: €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day, including skipper, drinks, and VAT. For the Mangusta 80 (white or grey), the minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719, with a jet ski included free. All other boats (e.g., Ferretti 94, Pershing 46, Lagoon 380) are priced on request via WhatsApp—just ask and we’ll confirm availability.

What’s Included on Every Charter

No hidden extras. Every boat includes:

  • Licensed skipper (handles everything)
  • Fuel and insurance
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (nuts, fruit, crisps)
  • Safety equipment and Spanish IVA (21%)

You can also bring your own recovery drinks or protein shakes—just keep them in a cooler.

Best Recovery Itineraries from Puerto Banús

Depart from Puerto Banús and head east towards Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés—two calm, shallow coves ideal for gentle swimming. Or cruise west to Cabopino and Estepona, where you can anchor off sandy beaches. If you prefer a longer trip, continue to Sotogrande for a relaxed lunch at a beach club. Your skipper will tailor the route to your energy levels.

Recovery Tips Onboard

  • Hydrate constantly—water is provided, but add electrolytes if needed.
  • Do light stretching on the deck; avoid deep stretching immediately after the race.
  • Use the swim stops to float, not to do laps.
  • Apply sunscreen religiously—your skin is sensitive post-race.
  • Nap in the shade; the gentle rocking is surprisingly therapeutic.

Booking Your Recovery Day

Ready to treat yourself? Browse our full fleet and pick your ideal recovery vessel. For Tier A boats, you can book directly online. For other boats, message us on WhatsApp for pricing and availability. We recommend booking at least 2-3 weeks before Ironman 2051 to secure your preferred time slot. After the race, you’ll have a seamless, stress-free day on the water.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best boat for a small Ironman recovery group?

For a group of up to 5, the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) are perfect. Both depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper, drinks, and snacks. If you have up to 8 people, the Bandido (11.5m) offers more space. For larger groups of 10-12, consider the Azimut 39 or Fairline Targa.

Can I swim in the sea after the Ironman?

Absolutely. The sea around Marbella is calm and warm, especially in summer. Your skipper can anchor in sheltered spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where you can float, swim gently, and let your muscles recover. Always listen to your body and stay hydrated.

Are drinks and food included on the charter?

Yes, every charter includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. For deeper recovery, you can bring your own electrolytes or protein bars—just let the crew know. No extra charges for standard inclusions.

How far in advance should I book the yacht after Ironman 2051?

Book at least 2-3 weeks ahead, especially if you want a specific boat like the Mangusta 80 or a longer 8-hour charter. Ironman week brings many visitors to Marbella, so early booking ensures availability and better time slots.

What if I'm too tired to sail?

You don't need to do anything—our licensed skippers handle all navigation. You can simply lie on the deck, enjoy the views of La Concha, and let the gentle motion of the boat aid your recovery. No experience required.

Are there any extra fees for fuel or taxes?

No. Fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%) are all included in the quoted price. The only optional extras are things like a private chef or watersports (except the free jet ski on Mangusta 80 charters).

Make your Ironman 2051 finish even more special with a marbella yacht charter ironman 2051 recovery day. It’s the reward you’ve earned—book your yacht today and let the Mediterranean do the rest.
